body:
## Summary
The command bar is the fastest bulk-adverse surface in the product (one typed line rejects and emails a cohort), and it is the one door that bypasses `runPipelineEntryAction`. Route its execute loop through that core so every command-bar decision is sealed, names its actor, egresses to the ATS, expires the group-eval cache, and inherits the offer/terminal guards the single and batch routes already enforce.

## Description
`pipeline-entry-action.ts` was built so the per-entry and batch routes 'can never diverge on the guards that matter'. `command/execute.ts` predates that and still calls `actOnPipelineEntry` directly. Concretely, a `reject below 40%` today writes N rejections with **no decision_records row** (the tamper-evident chain shows nothing), a **NULL actor** on the event, **no `candidate.rejected` ATS event** and a stale group-eval cache; an `advance top N` on a composed board can **bare-advance onto the terminal column** (phantom hire, onboarding fires) or **destroy a drafted offer** on an axis with no offer column - the exact two defects `runPipelineEntryAction` was fixed for. The move: (1) `EntryActionInput` gains optional `via: "command_bar"` + `threshold`, which set the seal's `policyVersion` and decisive inputs; (2) `runPipelineEntryAction` guards the post-commit `dispatchRejection` (records `rejection_comms_failed`, answers 200 with `commsFailed: true`, still egresses and expires) - which also stops the single route answering 500 for a reject that committed; (3) `executeCommandTargets` takes an injectable `runAction` (default `runPipelineEntryAction`) and maps its result codes into the existing buckets: 200 -> count (+commsFailed), 422 `PIPELINE_TERMINAL_NOT_ADVANCE` -> heldAtOffer, other non-200 / throw -> failed. advance_top holds any target carrying `offer_review` BEFORE calling (the bar's preview promises 'up to Offer', never an unattended offer extension).

## Flow
route.ts resolves `origin` + `ws` -> executeCommandTargets({kind, threshold, targets, axis, ws, origin}) -> per target: runPipelineEntryAction({id, action, expectedStage: e.stage, detail, via, threshold}) -> CAS write in the store -> seal (actor from session) -> rejection comm (guarded) -> ATS egress -> cache expiry -> bucketed result.

## Expected impact
Every bulk adverse action from the bar becomes auditable and attributable (bulk-adverse-action-governance: the approval's actor is the approver). One class of defect closes structurally: a guard added to the entry-action core now reaches all three bulk doors instead of two. Board integrity on composed axes: no phantom hires, no destroyed offer drafts from the bar.

## Evaluation
Claim: the command bar writes only through runPipelineEntryAction, and inherits its seal, actor, egress and outcome guards.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass.
After: 7 of 7.
Method: gate - node:test cases in command-one-core.test.ts (real unit DB, composed axes via setDecisionConfig), command-execution-counts.test.ts (injected runAction), pipeline-entry-action.test.ts (comms-throw case).
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract

title: Undo a command-bar reject wave: restore the exact set where they stood
acceptance: planWaveReversal({status:'rejected', eventsNewestFirst:[{kind:'rejected', detail:'Command bar: below 40%'}]}, 40) -> { restorable: true, notified: false }

planWaveReversal({status:'rejected', eventsNewestFirst:[{kind:'rejection_sent'}, {kind:'rejected', detail:'Command bar: below 40%'}]}, 40) -> { restorable: true, notified: true } (the letter event after the reject does not block the undo, it is reported)

planWaveReversal({status:'rejected', eventsNewestFirst:[{kind:'rejected', detail:'Recruiter note'}]}, 40) -> { restorable: false, reason: 'not_this_wave' } (a hand reject or another wave is never undone by this door)
planWaveReversal({status:'active', eventsNewestFirst:[{kind:'reinstated'}, {kind:'rejected', detail:'Command bar: below 40%'}]}, 40) -> { restorable: false, reason: 'not_rejected' }

restoreCommandRejection on a real unit-DB entry command-rejected at 'Interview' -> status 'active', stage STILL 'Interview' (not the screened landing column), a 'reinstated' pipeline_events row with non-null actor, and a decision_records row kind 'reinstated', reasonCode 'command_wave_reversed', inputs.threshold 40

reverseCommandWave(ids=[a,b,c,x], threshold 40) where a,b wave-rejected (b notified), c since moved by a human, x belongs to another workspace -> { restored: 2, notified: 1, skipped: 2 }; c and x rows byte-identical after the call
a second reverseCommandWave with the same ids -> { restored: 0, skipped: 4 } (idempotent: the undo cannot churn or double-seal)
execute.ts builds its reject detail with commandRejectDetail(threshold) from pipeline-command.ts, the same function planWaveReversal matches against (one literal, cannot drift)
premise: app/features/hiring/pipeline/CommandBar.tsx:68-79 - after a confirmed command the bar enters phase 'done' and only paints counts; app/features/hiring/pipeline/CommandBar.tsx:195-202 are count lines with no action on any of them
app/features/hiring/pipeline/CommandBar.tsx:56-58 - the client already holds the full reviewed id set (result.matchedIds) at confirm time, so the wave's members are known without a new server read
app/api/pipeline/command/execute.ts:64 - every command-bar reject writes the detail `Command bar: below ${threshold}%`, a stable marker an undo can match on
app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:3164 - a reject sets status='rejected' and leaves `stage` untouched, so the stage a candidate stood on survives the rejection and can be restored exactly
app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:1332 - the only existing reversal, reinstatePipelineEntry, lands the candidate on screenedLandingStage, i.e. an Interview-stage reject comes back two columns earlier

app/api/pipeline/[id]/route.ts:112 - reinstate is per-entry only, and its seal at app/api/pipeline/[id]/route.ts:127-128 hardcodes 'Auto-rejection reversed' / restoredStage 'Screened' - wrong for a human command wave
app/_lib/comms-status.ts:35 - OUTBOX_STATUSES has no withdrawn state, so a sent rejection letter cannot be recalled; the undo must say who was already told rather than imply it was unsent
rollback: Additive: a new route, a new store function beside reinstatePipelineEntry, a pure planner and a done-panel button. Reverting the series removes the door; no existing row shape, status value or event kind changes ('reinstated' already exists).
runner_up: The preview states who the cutoff left out: the count of unscored active candidates reject_below silently skips, and the tie straddling the advance-top-N boundary resolved toward the candidate.
body:
## Summary
A typed `reject below 40%` rejects and emails a whole cohort in one confirm, and today the only way back is one candidate at a time through a door built for auto-rejections that also drops them to the Screened column. Put an **Undo this wave** action on the command bar's done panel that restores exactly the wave's still-untouched members to the stage they stood on, seals each reversal to the person undoing it, and says plainly how many had already been sent the letter.

## Description
The governing standard (bulk-adverse-action-governance) holds that a bulk adverse action is defensible only if it is reversible by a cheap standing mechanism, and that a reversal is a NEW decision sealed to the reversing human, never an overwrite. kp has the reverse half for single auto-rejections only. This card adds the bulk human half:
- `pipeline-command.ts` (pure): `commandRejectDetail(threshold)` (the one literal execute.ts writes) and `planWaveReversal(snapshot, threshold)` -> `{restorable, notified, reason}` over the entry's status + newest-first events: restorable only when status is `rejected` and the newest non-comms event is this wave's `rejected` row; `notified` when a `rejection_sent` follows it.
- `db/pipeline.ts`: `restoreCommandRejection(id, ws, {threshold, actorRef})` - IMMEDIATE tx, re-reads status + events inside the lock, runs the planner, `UPDATE ... SET status='active' WHERE status='rejected'` (changes===0 -> skip), stage untouched, records `reinstated` with the actor.
- `command/reverse.ts`: `reverseCommandWave(ids, threshold, ws, actor, deps)` - per-id isolation, seals `reinstated` / `command_wave_reversed`, buckets restored / notified / skipped.
- `command/reverse/route.ts`: operator + `pipeline:write` gated like the command route; body `{ids, threshold}` (cap 200).
- `CommandBar.tsx`: the done panel of a reject_below keeps the confirmed id set and offers **Undo this wave**; the result line reads 'Restored 11 · 9 had already been sent the rejection letter - follow up with them · 1 had moved since and was left alone'.

## Flow
confirm reject_below -> done panel (counts + Undo) -> POST /api/pipeline/command/reverse {ids, threshold} -> per id: restoreCommandRejection (lock, plan, CAS write, event) -> seal reinstated -> response {restored, notified, skipped} -> bar paints the truthful outcome and refreshes the board via onExecuted().

## Expected impact
The single most destructive recruiter action gets a one-click, audited way back while the recruiter is still looking at it: a mistyped threshold (40 for 60) stops being a manual 30-candidate repair that also regresses everyone to Screened. The undo never claims the letter was recalled - it names who needs a human follow-up.

## Evaluation
Claim: a command-bar reject wave is reversible from the bar, exactly, attributably and idempotently.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test over planWaveReversal (pure), restoreCommandRejection + reverseCommandWave on the unit DB (cross-workspace + idempotency cases), plus the literal-sharing check.
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract
